issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Rideable interface (with messageOnRide()), but the solution repository uses a different interface name (Mountable) for the ride functionality and leaves Rideable.java empty. Pig and Seal in the solution implement Mountable rather than Rideable. This naming mismatch between Rideable (problem/template) and Mountable (solution) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students and break compatibility with code/tests that refer to Rideable.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ride-related interface name consistent across all artifacts. Replace Mountable with Rideable in the solution: either remove Mountable and implement Rideable.java with the method String messageOnRide(), and update Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable, or rename Rideable.java to provide the expected interface and ensure its signature matches the problem statement (messageOnRide()). This keeps the template, problem statement, and solution aligned.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template code refer to the ride-related interface as 'Rideable', but the solution implementation uses the name 'Mountable' for the same conceptual interface (and the concrete classes implement Mountable). This mismatch (Rideable vs Mountable) creates confusion: students are instructed to implement/use Rideable, the template's Main references Rideable, yet the reference solution provides Mountable and classes implementing Mountable. This makes it unclear which interface name students should use and breaks the direct mapping from requirements to the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure a single consistent interface name for the ride-related concept across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution's Mountable interface and all its usages to Rideable (update Mountable.java → Rideable.java and have Pig/Seal implement Rideable), or (B) change the problem statement and template references to use Mountable. Keep the method signature messageOnRide() unchanged so behavior remains consistent.
